sentences.text: Bothriolepis is characterized by bony plates covering its head and the anterior part of its trunk.
It had a keyhole-shaped opening on the top of its head for eyes and nostrils and a mouth opening on the lower side near the front.
The animal possessed a preorbital recess, a bone partition below the eye and nostril openings that enclosed the nasal capsules.
In adults, Bothriolepis had two separate jaw halves that were functionally independent.
The genus Bothriolepis was described by Eichwald in 1840.
Bothriolepis canadensis was first described in 1880 by J.F. Whiteaves.
More than two hundred individuals of Bothriolepis were found packed closely together at the Catskill Formation site.
The species B. nitida and B. minor were described from the Catskill Formation site.
Most species of Bothriolepis were small, benthic freshwater detritivores averaging about 30 cm in length.
Researchers suggest Bothriolepis used its spike-like pectoral fins to lift its armored body off the bottom.
Bothriolepis possessed a specialized complex spiral valve in its digestive system, similar to that found in some sharks.
Robert Denison published a paper exploring the soft anatomy and organs of Bothriolepis.
Bothriolepis is classified within the class Placodermi.
Bothriolepis is classified within the placoderm order Antiarchi.
Bothriolepis fossils are found in strata dating from 387 to 360 million years ago.
Bothriolepis lived during the Late Middle Devonian, approximately 387 to 360 million years ago.
Bothriolepis inhabited near-shore marine and freshwater environments across all paleocontinents.
Bothriolepis fossils have been found in Asia, Europe, Australia, Africa, North America, and South America.
It is unclear exactly when gnathostomes emerged, though the fossil record suggests the Early Palaeozoic era.
It is debated whether Bothriolepis had a notochord, as the trunk outline suggests one but no direct evidence exists due to soft tissue decay.
It is debated whether the ventral sacs of Bothriolepis functioned as lungs that allowed the animal to travel on land.
Not all paleontologists agree with the 1941 interpretation that Bothriolepis possessed lungs.
